Typed frames over a local socket

Notes from wiring a browser tool to a local server, and what broke along the way.

The short version: share the schemas, check the origin, and keep the catalog hashed.

The protocol

  • Both server and browser share the same Zod schemas and wire frames (session.hello, session.ready, tool.request, tool.progress, tool.cancel, tool.response), plus a hash of the tool catalog so version mismatches fail right away.
  • Even on 127.0.0.1, you cannot leave the door open. The WebSocket upgrade checks an Origin allow-list so random tabs cannot hijack your session.

Every frame is validated on both ends before anything acts on it.

The places query

The map view asks for nearby places with one join against the spatial index:

SELECT p.id, p.label, p.is_public, p.lat, p.lng FROM places p JOIN places_rtree rp ON rp.id = p.rowid;

It returns in a few milliseconds even with a large table.

What is left

Reconnects still drop the in-flight request.

That is the next thing to fix.
